name_note: NCBI labels these genomes Candidatus Nanosynbacter; the genus was validly published as Nanosynbacter, whose described species Nanosynbacter lyticus is the long-studied strain TM7x.

sentences.text: It replicates as an obligate epibiont on the surface of another oral species and was obtained by directed cultivation from human oral samples.
The organism belongs to the Saccharibacteria phylum within the Candidate Phyla Radiation, whose members are described as ubiquitous in the human oral microbiome.
Lacking the ability to make its own amino acids, vitamins or cell wall precursors, it must parasitize other oral bacteria and can kill its bacterial host.
A study of saliva and plaque from children in a South China population reported Saccharibacteria as a caries-associated phylum in children.
